card.headline: Brooklyn is the fastest-growing family with first-time Gen Z customers that still has stock, so it could keep that growth going while Tabby is short.

items.text: First-time Gen Z customers rose from {seg_customers_ly} to {seg_customers_ty} and brought {seg_growth_share} of all sales growth.
Brooklyn drew {pick_customers_ty} first-time Gen Z customers against {pick_customers_ly} last year, adding {pick_diff} in sales from them.
Tabby ({lead_diff}) and Pillow Tabby ({lead2_diff}) gained more from these customers but have only {lead_cover} and {lead2_cover} weeks of stock left.
Brooklyn has {pick_cover} weeks of stock ({pick_stock} units) against {pick_cover_ly} last year, and its total sales are up {pick_sales_yoy}.
{pick_store_share} of first-time Gen Z purchases of Brooklyn were made in stores.
Gen Z shoppers who come in for Tabby may choose Brooklyn instead if it sits next to it, which would keep first-time Gen Z growth going while Tabby is restocked.
Feature Brooklyn beside Tabby in a small set of stores and on the online pages Gen Z shoppers visit, for the next few weeks.
Watch first-time Gen Z customers buying Brooklyn each week in those stores against similar stores without the change.
Stock and traffic by store, to know where Brooklyn is available and where Gen Z shoppers come in.
Promotion and price history, since part of Brooklyn's growth may come from discounts.
The base is small, {pick_customers_ty} customers, so treat this as a test to run rather than a forecast.
